senses.gloss: m. = פֵּירָא, fruit.—Pl. פּוֹרַיָּא, פּוֹרִין, פּוֹרֵי. Ruth R. introd. (ref. to תפיל, Prov. XIX, 15) כמד״א נפל שעריהון דפ׳ as you say, the price of fruits has fallen (meaning, fruits are plentiful).
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:4:7-8">Y. Taan. III, 66ᵈ</cite> top <he>איתון חמון פ׳ דשמש</he> come and see the fruits of the sun (of a hot and dry year).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 71">Gen. R. s. 71</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="P00622"><he>עיניו</he></cite> <cite ref="Job 36:7">Job XXXVI, 7</cite>) <he>כאינש דאמר עיניהון דפוֹרַיָּה</he> (not <he>עינוהי</he>) as a man says, the eyes (prospects) of the fruits (hopes of success; Midr. Sam. ch. XXVIII <he>עייניהון קפידיהין</he>, v. <cite ref="S01732"><he>קְפֵידָא</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 2:11:4">Y. B. Mets. II, end, 8ᵈ</cite> <he>בריך רחמנא דחמי לי פ׳ עד וכ׳</he> blessed be the Merciful who made me see fruits (success of my pupil), while I am alive; a. e.
